answer: Duplicate identities are rejected because forging a fresh key costs real compute and locked stake, while cloning an existing one requires breaking its cipher. Each new agent must stake a bond and solve a unique proof-of-work tied to its identity, then broadcast a whisper of its registration across peers who verify the cipher signature. Like ripples crossing a vast ocean, every sybil attempt spends scarce resources for negligible influence, making mass fake identities economically irrational and self-defeating.
